key_insight: Multi-agent reinforcement learning discovers non-intuitive rendezvous behaviors in vortical flows that exploit fluid kinematics to prevent agents from getting trapped in separate vortices.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests that swarm coordination in complex fluids can be improved by planning rendezvous in weak-deformation regions and using learned policies that transfer across flow conditions and swarm sizes.
method: Train a multi-agent reinforcement learning policy for rendezvous in vortical flows
Compare learned strategies against a naive direct-navigation baseline
Extract a heuristic strategy and analyze fluid deformation using finite-time Lyapunov exponents
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MARL strategies significantly improve rendezvous rate over naive navigation and transfer across vortex intensity, vortex scale, and swarm size variations.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurately modeling flow structures; policies and heuristics could degrade in strongly time-varying or poorly resolved fluid fields.
paper_title: Multi-agent rendezvous in fluid flows via reinforcement learning
